nodes.title: Universal motivic Chern classes
nodes.statement: Construct the natural motivic Chern operations c_{j,m}: K_m(X) → H^{2j−m}(X,Z(j)) for j≥1 and m≥0 from the universal classes on BGL. On K_0 these are the geometric Chern classes of S.7; for m>0 they are homomorphisms. The construction is through the actual K-space and the motivic cycle complex, with a coherent extension to relative diagrams required for the comparison below. Set c_{0,0}=rank and c_{0,m}=0 for m>0 as separate conventions. No additivity of c_{j,0} for j>1 is asserted.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field; X is smooth quasi-projective and of finite type over k, of dimension d. Disconnected X is treated componentwise.
m and j are nonnegative integers. Rational coefficients mean tensoring the integral groups with Q, not replacing the integral cycle complex by its cohomology before deriving sections.
proofSteps: For a representation G→GL(E), form the projective bundle over the simplicial scheme B•G. Define its Chern classes by the coefficients of the monic relation for ξ=c_1(O(1)); the projective-bundle basis determines the coefficients uniquely. Use M.4 projective bundles and the requested simplicial descent adapter.

The localization sequence for a projective bundle associated to an extension proves Whitney; splitting into lines proves the tensor-polynomial identities. In the Whitney argument use the closed bundle P(F′) as the Gysin source, and the homogeneous polynomial C_E(T)=Σ_{i=0}^rank(E)(−1)^i c_i(E)T^(rank(E)−i), with c_0=1: C_F=C_F′ C_F″. These correct the displays in E-M6-2. The classes are universal geometric classes, not characteristic classes assigned separately to each K-group.

Evaluate the stable universal class on the plus/completed K-space, using the Hurewicz and Dold–Kan construction of K-book V.11.3, V.11.6–11.8. Zariski descent glues the affine evaluation. Its π_m action has the indicated cohomological degree.

Compare the degree-zero evaluation with the S.7 geometric classes. For the relative cubical comparison retain the diagrams, homotopies and support maps through derived sections; their existence is the precise GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.2 / SF.5 request, recorded as gap G2. Objectwise group maps are insufficient.

sources.match: Universal characteristic classes induce higher operations; projective bundles supply the motivic classes and the degree-zero/units normalization.

Over a perfect field, maps from Z×Gr to a motivic Eilenberg–MacLane space are determined by the corresponding natural K_0-to-Chow operations. This is a source check on uniqueness, not an assertion that K-endomorphism uniqueness alone supplies these target maps.

acceptance: The operation has a specified universal class and a derived evaluation, not merely the correct codomain.

nodes.title: Normalized higher Chern character
nodes.statement: Define ch_{j,m}:K_m(X)_Q→H^{2j−m}(X,Q(j)). For m=0 use the existing S.7 character: ch_{0,0}=rank and ch_{j,0}=N_j(c_1,…,c_j)/j! for j≥1. For m>0 set ch_{0,m}=0 and ch_{j,m}=a_j c_{j,m} for j≥1, where a_j=(−1)^{j−1}/(j−1)!. The auxiliary scalar function a: N→Q has a_0=0 solely to encode the m>0 convention. It is not the K_0 rank character. The total character has finitely many nonzero components, j≤d+m.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field; X is smooth quasi-projective and of finite type over k, of dimension d. Disconnected X is treated componentwise.
m and j are nonnegative integers. Rational coefficients mean tensoring the integral groups with Q, not replacing the integral cycle complex by its cohomology before deriving sections.
proofSteps: Import the Newton-polynomial character in degree zero from S.7. Positive loop degree kills decomposable universal cohomology classes under evaluation on a suspension, leaving N_j=(-1)^{j−1}j c_j; division by j! gives the stated a_j.
Use rational scalar multiplication on the homomorphisms c_{j,m} for m>0. Treat weight zero separately: the higher homology of the constant weight-zero cycle complex is zero.
The bound CH^j(X,m)=0 for j>d+m follows because X×Δ^m has dimension d+m; use M.4 and the motivic comparison. Thus the total character lies in a direct sum in each degree.
The light scalar function and its cancellation identities are statable at the pins. They check normalization only; they provide none of the missing motivic carriers.

sources.match: The universal Chern product rule fixes the sign and factorial on positive-degree classes. Newton polynomials give the degree-zero character.

nodes.title: Products and Adams operations for the higher character
nodes.statement: For admitted X and x∈K_m(X)_Q, y∈K_n(X)_Q, ch_{r,m+n}(xy)=Σ_{i+j=r} ch_{i,m}(x)∪ch_{j,n}(y). The same formula holds for external products on X×Y. The character preserves the unit, is Q-linear, commutes with pullback, and satisfies ch_{j,m}(ψ^k x)=k^j ch_{j,m}(x) for integers k≥2. The cohomological cup sign is (−1)^{mn}, since 2i−m and 2j−n have parity m and n. Consequently ch_{j,m} vanishes on an Adams weight i≠j.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field; X is smooth quasi-projective and of finite type over k, of dimension d. Disconnected X is treated componentwise.
m and j are nonnegative integers. Rational coefficients mean tensoring the integral groups with Q, not replacing the integral cycle complex by its cohomology before deriving sections.
Use the actual tensor product on scheme K-theory and the cycle-complex cup product imported from S.6 and M.4.
proofSteps: Start with the universal tensor/Newton identity giving ch(E⊗F)=ch(E)ch(F) on K_0. Lift this two-operand identity to maps into motivic Eilenberg–MacLane spaces using the several-operand extension immediately before Riou Proposition 6.2.2.1, then evaluate on S^m∧S^n and the actual K tensor product. This identifies the mixed and two-positive-degree products with their motivic cup products, subject to G2. Agreement of group operations on K_0 alone would not justify this step.

Equivalently, derive the two-positive-degree Chern coefficient −(i+j−1)!/((i−1)!(j−1)!) from that universal tensor identity after reduced evaluation kills the decomposable terms in each factor; multiplying by a_{i+j} gives a_i a_j. K-book V.11.3 explicitly states the diagonal graded-ring case, not the whole arbitrary-weight dg-coefficient formula. Use its V.11.5(4) tensor identity and the motivic uniqueness argument for the general case. M.4 supplies the diagonal/external-product comparison, and Levine Theorem 5.2 fixes the higher Chow sign.

For Adams compatibility, lift the universal Newton operations through the same completed/sheaf K model as S.6. Riou’s motivic uniqueness checks this for maps into motivic Eilenberg–MacLane spaces, not just endomorphisms of K. The required coherent class evaluation is G2.
If x has weight i, Q-linearity and the last identity give (2^i−2^j)ch_{j,m}(x)=0. Distinct powers of 2 are invertible in Q, so the off-weight component vanishes.

sources.match: The universal tensor identity supplies the character product calculation; V.11.3 and V.11.13 check its diagonal specialization. The arbitrary-weight higher product uses the several-operand motivic lifting, rather than a broader reading of V.11.3.
Products on higher Chow groups are functorial and graded commutative in the higher Chow degree.

sources.locator: Theorem 6.2.1.2, pp.31–32; several-operand extension preceding Proposition 6.2.2.1, p.32; Definition 6.2.3.9 and Remark 6.2.3.10, pp.34–35
sources.match: Motivic-target uniqueness, including several operands, lifts the degree-zero tensor identity; the stable rational character and its Adams components fix the higher normalization. The S.6 K-endomorphism uniqueness theorem alone has the wrong target.

acceptance: For a line bundle L and a unit u, ch(Lu)=exp(c_1(L))ch(u), in the finite degreewise range.
Check the unit in degree zero and the sign under exchange of two degree-one factors.
Adams eigenspace vanishing does not by itself prove equality with the edge comparison.

nodes.title: Gamma filtration and homotopy-coniveau filtration
nodes.statement: For smooth quasi-projective X over a perfect field and m≥0, write F_HC^p K_m(X)=im(π_m K^(p)(X)→K_m(X)). Use the full weighted gamma filtration from S.6/S.7, not the subgroup generated by single gamma operations. Then F_γ^p K_m(X)_Q=F_HC^p K_m(X)_Q=⊕_{j≥p}K_m(X)_Q^(j). These filtrations vanish for p>d+m and start at the whole group for p=0. Their associated graded comparisons are the identity on the common Adams eigenspace. In degree zero this recovers S.7/gamma-chow-comparison.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field; X is smooth quasi-projective and of finite type over k, of dimension d. Disconnected X is treated componentwise.
m and j are nonnegative integers. Rational coefficients mean tensoring the integral groups with Q, not replacing the integral cycle complex by its cohomology before deriving sections.
proofSteps: Transport the Levine/FS filtration to the chosen homotopy-coniveau tower by the augmentation-compatible global-model comparison; this use of G1 is required, not supplied by an E₂ identification. Use Levine’s relative K_0 argument, Lemma 13.3, Theorem 13.10 and Corollary 13.11: the Friedlander–Suslin comparison from multirelative K_0 is onto and preserves the K_0(X)-lambda structure; lift weighted gamma expressions to that relative K_0. Move their Grassmannian support into facewise codimension at least p, giving F_γ^p⊂F_HC^p.

For the field case use the semilocal Grassmannian part of the proof on p.66: over an infinite field move by the product of special linear groups, and over a finite field use transfers from extensions of coprime degrees. The gluing across closed points of a one-dimensional base is not invoked. This is the field adaptation advertised in the introduction, p.2; Corollary 13.11 is printed for a one-dimensional base.

The inherited connectivity bound π_m K^(p)(X)=0 for p>d+m makes F_HC finite. The inclusion therefore proves finite length of the full F_γ in this scope. The implication is from the relative moving comparison, not from operationwise gamma vanishing.

Adams acts on gr_γ^p and gr_HC^p by k^p. Apply the finite simultaneous eigenspace/projector argument of Lemma 14.6 and Theorem 14.7 with corrected indices and inclusion direction (inherited sourceIssues E6–E8). Every actual weight j lies at filtration index j in both filtrations. This proves rational equality and compatibility of graded identifications. In importing the filtered Adams theorem, use only its generic supported K_0/Koszul weight calculation; its citation of S.7 is not permission to assume a higher gamma-filtration isomorphism whose boundedness is being proved here.

sources.locator: §13.1–13.3, pp.59–61; Theorem 13.10 and Corollary 13.11, pp.65–68; Theorem 14.5, pp.70–71; Lemma 14.6 and Theorem 14.7, pp.71–74; field scope in introduction, p.2
sources.match: A relative K_0 moving argument includes the gamma filtration in homotopy coniveau. Finite Adams filtrations then identify them rationally. The field proof uses the Grassmannian/transfer portion of the argument; the printed general statement also treats a one-dimensional base.

acceptance: On K_0(P²)_Q the classes 1, u=[O(1)]−1 and u² give F¹=(u,u²), F²=(u²), F³=0 in either filtration.
On K_1(F)_Q the unit classes have filtration one, not filtration zero as their only nonzero graded degree.
For m=0, import the existing S.7 Chow comparison rather than defining a second ordinary Chow filtration.
Do not assert the integral equality, a supported variant with bound d+m, or a gamma bound obtained only by checking γ^r(x)=0.

nodes.title: Relative cycle normalization of the character
nodes.statement: Let X be smooth quasi-projective over a perfect field. For j,m≥0 let cyc_{j,m}: CH^j_□(X,m)_Q→K_m(X)_Q^(j) be Levine’s cycle isomorphism. Its construction uses multirelative K_0 on X×□^m and supported structure-sheaf classes, with projection to the generalized ψ^k characteristic summand of index j in the relative/support diagram, identified with the genuine weight-j summand after comparison with K_m(X); a raw structure-sheaf class need not have pure weight j. Transport the cubical group to CH^j(X,m) by M.4. With the same ordering of cube faces and the corresponding suspension signs, ch_{j,m}∘cyc_{j,m}=id and ch_{i,m}∘cyc_{j,m}=0 for i≠j. This identifies actual maps, including j=0, rather than just two abstractly isomorphic rational vector spaces.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field; X is smooth quasi-projective and of finite type over k, of dimension d. Disconnected X is treated componentwise.
m and j are nonnegative integers. Rational coefficients mean tensoring the integral groups with Q, not replacing the integral cycle complex by its cohomology before deriving sections.

Both cycle and K-theory use the fixed ordered iterated-fibre convention for the cube. The supported universal character / relative-diagram adapter G2–G3 is a prerequisite; ordinary K_0 classes after forgetting supports cannot replace it.
proofSteps: Levine Lemma 2.1 and the construction preceding Lemma 2.2 uses the rational characteristic-summand projection in its supported and relative cycle maps; retain it before passing to the weight-j target. Theorem 3.1 compares the cubical cycle group with the weight-j summand of multirelative K_0, identified with K_m(X) by homotopy invariance. Theorem 3.3 proves Zariski Mayer–Vietoris descent, and Theorem 3.4 supplies supported/localization compatibility. Use the imported finite rational Adams splitting for the final projector on K_m(X).

Before forgetting supports, the leading supported Chern class of the perfect resolution of an integral codimension-j cycle is (−1)^{j−1}(j−1)![Z], with lower supported classes zero. This is the normalization requested from SF.5 and already required by S.7/chern-class-of-subvariety. Extend it to the relative cube with specified face nullhomotopies; this extension is G3, not a consequence of agreement in ordinary CH(X).

Apply the universal Newton character to the relative class. The leading supported formula is unchanged by the weight-j projector because the character is Adams compatible; the projection removes the other weights. Pass through the ordered loop comparison: decomposable terms vanish in positive loop degree and a_j cancels the leading signed factorial. At m=0, ch_j([O_Z])=[Z] is a leading-term statement, while the pure-weight inverse is pr_j[O_Z]. For j=0 use rank and the acyclicity in positive degree.

The off-weight terms vanish by higher-character-structure. M.4’s simplicial/cubical comparison and the same ordered suspension convention yield the assertion on the chosen motivic complex. Until G2–G3 are supplied this is a planned comparison, not a verified closed proof.

sources.locator: Lemma 2.1, construction preceding Lemma 2.2, and Lemma 2.2 with proof, pp.258–265; Theorem 3.1 and proof, pp.276–278; Theorems 3.3–3.4, pp.279–284
sources.match: The cycle map includes a projection to the required rational characteristic summand. Theorem 3.3 gives Zariski descent; Theorem 3.4 gives the supported/localization form. The underlying structure-sheaf map alone is not the pure-weight isomorphism.
The universal higher Chern evaluation has the signed factorial on symbols, fixing the normalization used in the relative comparison.

acceptance: For a divisor D at m=0, cyc_{1,0}([D])=pr_1[O_D]; ch_1([O_D])=[D] records its leading term only. On P², with u=[O(1)]−1 and h=c_1(O(1)), a hyperplane has [O_D]=u−u², ch([O_D])=h−h²/2 and pr_1[O_D]=u−u²/2, whose total character is h. This detects omission of the weight projector.
For a unit at m=j=1 the two maps are inverse with no sign.
For a triple Milnor symbol, the Chern factor is +2 and the normalized composite is the identity.
Record and check the relative supported extension G3; neither abstract Adams splitting nor the existence of cyc proves this composite formula.

nodes.title: Universal character and motivic edge comparison
nodes.statement: For X smooth quasi-projective over a perfect field, the existing rational-weight-comparison θ_{j,m}:K_m(X)_Q^(j)≅H^{2j−m}(X,Q(j)), obtained from the homotopy-coniveau tower with its normalized cycle layer, is precisely ch_{j,m} restricted to weight j. Equivalently, ch_{j,m}=θ_{j,m}∘pr_j on K_m(X)_Q. For the S.7 abstract gamma character, composing with gr_γ^j≅gr_HC^j≅H^{2j−m}(X,Q(j)) gives the same map. The identity at m=0 is the S.7 geometric character and gamma–Chow comparison.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field; X is smooth quasi-projective and of finite type over k, of dimension d. Disconnected X is treated componentwise.
m and j are nonnegative integers. Rational coefficients mean tensoring the integral groups with Q, not replacing the integral cycle complex by its cohomology before deriving sections.
The filtered global-model comparison is imported from M.6a; its remaining filtered and product coherence gaps G1 are not discharged by equality of E₂ pages.
proofSteps: Import the full filtered tower, augmentation, normalized layer equivalence and strong convergence; these already have node IDs in the accepted M.5d packet. Retain its finite Adams splitting and the canonical projection pr_j. There is no new spectral-sequence construction here.

Under the M.6a layer cycle normalization, the inverse of the rational edge map is the projected multirelative cycle class cyc_{j,m}. Verify this diagram at the support K_0 level and through the FS/Levine filtered comparison, retaining the Adams projector. This is the specific adapter added to the M.6a request; gap G1 prevents treating a group-level identification as the filtered comparison.
Apply relative-cycle-normalization: both θ and the universal ch are inverse to that actual cyc on the weight-j group. Off-weight vanishing then proves the equality on all K_m(X)_Q.

Use gamma-homotopy-coniveau-comparison and the S.7 gamma-character leading-term identity to identify the abstract gamma character with this map. This is a map comparison; equality of eigenvalues alone would still allow multiplication by any nonzero rational scalar.

sources.match: The normalized cycle class supplies a concrete inverse map to be compared, rather than an unnamed rational isomorphism.

sources.locator: Theorem 6.4.2, pp.35–37; Theorem 11.3.2 and Remark 11.3.4, pp.63–64
sources.match: The homotopy-coniveau layers identify with motivic complexes; this is the layer normalization on the tower route.
Adams weights split rational K, and universal motivic classes give the character whose actual normalization must be compared.

acceptance: At m=0 the diagram is the existing S.7 gamma/Chow diagram: [Z]↦[O_Z] modulo the next filtration is the inverse leading term, and [Z]↦pr_j[O_Z] is its pure-weight lift. For a hyperplane in P² this lift is u−u²/2, not u−u².
At j=m for a field the motivic edge map from Milnor K and ch have composite one after rationalization.
Do not infer this equality from collapse at E₂: a rescaled isomorphism has the same weights and dimension.
Prove the same comparison for the filtered FS model only after supplying its augmentation/layer-compatible zigzag.

nodes.title: Localization and the weight shift in residues
nodes.statement: The normalized character is a morphism of rational localization sequences in the admitted smooth quasi-projective pairs, with target the supported motivic cycle complex before purity. In particular let R be the local ring at a closed point x of a smooth curve over a perfect field, F its fraction field and κ its residue field. For m≥1,j≥1 the square with K_m(F)_Q→K_{m−1}(κ)_Q and H^{2j−m}(F,Q(j))→H^{2j−m−1}(κ,Q(j−1)) commutes, with vertical maps ch_{j,m} and ch_{j−1,m−1}. Thus the boundary carries Adams weight j to j−1. The residue convention has ∂_K(π)=1 and ∂_M({π,u})=ū for a uniformizer π and a unit u. At j=m=1 the lower character is rank. A general regular immersion requires its supported purity/normal-bundle Todd correction; uncorrected commutation with arbitrary proper pushforward is not asserted.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field; X is smooth quasi-projective and of finite type over k, of dimension d. Disconnected X is treated componentwise.
m and j are nonnegative integers. Rational coefficients mean tensoring the integral groups with Q, not replacing the integral cycle complex by its cohomology before deriving sections.

For the DVR specialization, take filtered colimits over smooth quasi-projective curve neighborhoods to define the essentially smooth local ring and fraction field; the finite-presentation cycle/perfect-complex continuity adapters are part of G2/G3.
Use the same fibre/cofiber boundary convention in K and cycle complexes. The conormal line of the DVR closed immersion is trivial, so its Todd factor is one.
proofSteps: Form K^Z(X)→K(X)→K(U) and the supported cycle triangle. Apply the coherent universal character to this diagram before taking homotopy/cohomology. The relative supported comparison of relative-cycle-normalization and Levine Theorem 3.4 identifies the resulting boundary maps.

Pass to the curve local ring and use codimension-one purity: K_{m−1}^x(R)≅K_{m−1}(κ), while H^{q+1}_x(R,Q(j))≅H^{q−1}(κ,Q(j−1)). The K purity identification shifts Adams weight by one; this is the S.6 residue-weight-shift convention.

The normal/conormal line is trivial at this point, so no higher Todd terms occur. Compute the sign with the M.4 cubical differential d=Σ_i(−1)^i(∂∞_i−∂0_i): a symbol with a uniformizer in its last coordinate has localization residue (−1)^{n−1} times the last-entry Milnor residue ∂^last{u_1,…,u_{n−1},π}={ū_1,…,ū_{n−1}}. Moving π to the first coordinate introduces the same sign, so the localization residue of {π,u_1,…,u_{n−1}} is positive. In particular δ{π,u}=ū, whereas the imported T.3 last-entry tame convention gives ∂^last{π,u}=ū^(−1). The square uses the localization convention of S.6, not an unidentified tame-symbol sign.

Transport the equality through chern-character-edge-comparison and the S.7 gamma-character comparison to obtain the residue-compatible weight dictionary used by arithmetic consumers. For higher codimension supported pairs retain supported classes until a precise Gysin/RR normalization is supplied.

acceptance: For R=k[t]_(t), the element t∈K_1(k(t)) has boundary 1∈K_0(k); its motivic residue is 1∈H^{0,0}(k,Q).

For {t,u}∈K_2(F), the residue under ch_{1,1} is ū, with the uniformizer first.
For {u,t}, graded commutativity changes the residue sign in additive notation.
The formulas do not apply unchanged to a general closed immersion with nontrivial normal bundle.

sourceIssues.printed: The first term of the localization display uses P(F″), although the stated closed immersion is P(F′) into P(F). The subsequent Chern polynomials omit the powers of ξ accompanying the lower Chern coefficients, including the displayed c_1 terms. (Description in our own words.)
sourceIssues.correction: The Gysin source is H^{2n−2n″,n′}(P(F′)); the weight n′ is unchanged. The open term remains P(F″). Write every rank-r Chern polynomial as C_E(T)=Σ_{i=0}^r(−1)^i c_i(E)T^(r−i), with c_0=1, and the factorization as C_F(T)=C_F′(T)C_F″(T).
sourceIssues.reason: The closed immersion has codimension n″, which determines its Gysin source, whereas homotopy invariance identifies the open complement with P(F″). Each polynomial term c_i(E)ξ^(r−i) has bidegree (2r,r); omitting ξ^(r−1) from c_1 gives a different bidegree when r>1. The initial monic relation on the same page already includes the required powers. Both corrections leave the intended Whitney formula intact.
